# Disclosure

> Show and hide content behind a summary. It's a native `<details>` with a few extras.

`<slab-disclosure>` · Disclosure · built on `<details>`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/disclosure/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/disclosure.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-disclosure label="Shipping">
  Orders ship within two business days.
</slab-disclosure>
```

Set `heading-level` to make the label a heading of that level, so screenreader users can jump between Disclosures by heading. The heading goes inside the `<summary>`, since a `<summary>` must be the first thing in a `<details>`. Most screenreaders read it as a heading there, but a few read only the `<summary>`'s button.

## Keyboard

| Key          | What it does                             |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| Enter, Space | Opens or closes it, as on a `<summary>`. |

## Elements

### `<slab-disclosure>`

Import `slab-elements/disclosure.js` to register it.

A disclosure with no visual styles, around a native `<details>`, so it opens, closes, and is read the way one is.

Nearly everything is the platform's. Enter and Space toggle it, find-in-page opens it to reveal a match, and its marker is the browser's until a design replaces it through `::part(summary)`. What Disclosure adds is a label, an `open` kept in step with the `<details>` however it was toggled, and a "toggle" event from the host.

`name` is passed to the `<details>`, but a name only groups `<details>` in the same tree, and each Disclosure's is in a shadow root of its own. So two Disclosures with the same `name` don't close each other. Grouping them is Accordion's job.

The label is text rather than a slot. A `<summary>` is a button to assistive technology, and a button's name is flattened to text regardless. Anything a design wants beside it, such as an icon, goes on through `::part(summary)`.

Set `heading-level` to make the label a heading of that level, as the APG's accordion puts each header in one, so screenreader users can jump between Disclosures by heading. The heading goes inside the `<summary>`, since a `<summary>` has to be the `<details>`'s first child. Most screenreaders read it as a heading there, though some read only the `<summary>`'s button.

#### Attributes

| Name               | Type                         | Default | Description                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `heading-level`    | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` |         | Makes the label a heading of this level, from 1 to 6.                                                                          |
| `label` (required) | `string`                     |         | Names it. It's the accessible name, and the visible label where there is one.                                                  |
| `name`             | `string`                     | `''`    | Groups it with every other Disclosure of the same name, so opening one closes the rest, as a native `<details>`'s `name` does. |
| `open`             | `boolean`                    | `false` | Whether it's open. Set it to open or close it.                                                                                 |

#### Methods

| Signature                             | Description                                      |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `click(): void`                       | Clicks it, as a native element's `click()` does. |
| `focus(options?: FocusOptions): void` | Focuses it, or the part of it that takes focus.  |

#### Events

| Name     | Type          | Description                                                                                                          |
| -------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `toggle` | `ToggleEvent` | When it opens or closes, as a `ToggleEvent` with `oldState` and `newState` that doesn't bubble, as a popover's does. |

#### Slots

| Name      | Type                | Description |
| --------- | ------------------- | ----------- |
| (default) | `Element \| string` |             |

#### CSS parts

| Name      | Description                                         |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `content` | The content revealed when open                      |
| `details` | The label, and the control that toggles the content |

#### CSS states

| Name           | Description      |
| -------------- | ---------------- |
| `:state(open)` | While it's open. |
